text: Patient presented with substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm. Troponin elevated, diagnosed with NSTEMI. Started on aspirin and heparin. Discharged in stable condition with cardiology follow-up.
Admitted with end stage renal disease and fluid overload. Tunneled catheter placed and hemodialysis initiated. Will continue outpatient dialysis three times weekly.
Presented with fever and productive cough. Chest x-ray showed right lower lobe infiltrate. Treated with IV antibiotics for pneumonia and transitioned to oral therapy.
Admitted with acute kidney injury in the setting of decompensated heart failure. Diuresis adjusted and renal function improved. Discharged on reduced diuretic dose.
Elective admission for management of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Rate control achieved with metoprolol. Anticoagulation started. No complications.
Observation stay for chest pain. Serial troponins negative and stress test unremarkable. Symptoms attributed to reflux. Discharged on a proton pump inhibitor.
Chronic kidney disease stage 5 with hyperkalemia and volume overload. Urgent dialysis performed with improvement in potassium. Arranged outpatient dialysis schedule.
Admitted for community acquired pneumonia. Blood glucose managed with insulin sliding scale. Completed antibiotic course and discharged home.
